tasks.brief:
Implementation constraints: Synchronous DOM edit in `src/static/catalog.js`. No async operations. Locate the `.finally` handler inside the model-load path (inside `fetchModels` or the change handler's load flow). The coder must edit the existing line that conditionally sets `modelSelect.disabled` based on `active.locked`. Replace that conditional with an unconditional `modelSelect.disabled = false`. Do not remove the `.finally` wrapper or the `modelSelect.disabled = true` at load start; only change the re-enable logic. Do not touch `window.Catalog`, `fetchModels` signature, or `refreshModels`.

Behavioral specification: When a model load completes (success or failure), the `#model-select` element must always be re-enabled, regardless of the thread's `.locked` field. The prior code read `active.locked` and disabled the selector for locked threads, which contradicts AC-133. The new code must unconditionally enable the selector.

Acceptance condition: The `#model-select` element is never disabled by JavaScript based on a thread's `.locked` field. Specifically, the `.finally` handler in the model-load path sets `modelSelect.disabled = false` unconditionally.

Implementation constraints: Synchronous DOM edit in `src/static/threads.js`. No async operations. Locate the function `restoreThreadModelState(thread)`. Remove the line `ms.disabled = !!thread.locked;` (or equivalent logic that disables the model selector based on `thread.locked`). Locate the function `lockThread(thread)`. Remove any block or line that sets `el('model-select').disabled = true` or `modelSelect.disabled = true` as a side effect of locking. The `thread.locked = true` assignment for persistence must remain if present, but no DOM side-effects are permitted.

Behavioral specification: `restoreThreadModelState` must not disable the `#model-select` element when restoring a thread that has `.locked = true`. `lockThread` must not disable the `#model-select` element when locking a thread. The invariant is that `#model-select` is never programmatically disabled based on per-thread state.

Acceptance condition: `restoreThreadModelState` contains no code that disables `#model-select` based on `thread.locked`. `lockThread` contains no code that disables `#model-select`. The selector remains enabled during thread switches and lock operations.
